newsitem.title: ITALY: IMF's Tanzi says BoI policy helping cut spending.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Tanzi says BoI policy helping cut spending.

text.p: Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio's tough monetary policy is helping limit Italy's public sector spending, said Vito Tanzi, director International Monetary Fund's (IMF) public finance department.
Tanzi, participating in a conference here on Italy's entry into the single European currency, said he was expressing his own personal opinion and not that of the IMF.

"With his policy, the governor has been one of the main figures in the process of correcting Italian public spending," he said. "Every time that I've seen a government forcing rates, the results have not been positive."
Fazio has kept the central bank's key discount rate firmly pegged at 6.75 percent since January despite a steady fall in headline inflation.
His caution has drawn criticism from industry and many economists who believe a chance to cut borrowing costs is being missed.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said he has never tried to pressure Fazio to cut the discount rate.
Tanzi said the fall in inflation was a fairly recent phenomenon. He also said the central bank had access to more up to date information and statistics.
Tanzi said he was confident European economic and monetary union (EMU) would start as planned.

"It will go ahead with Maastricht. When the finance ministers get together, they will close their eyes somewhat to existing problems and go on ahead. If current adjustments to public accounts are structural then, developments will be positive. If, however, they are just accounting corrections there will be big problems," he said.
